question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-3<X<3)=0.9232,$ find ${\sigma }^{2},$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9418\,$ | $\,0.9429\,$ | $\,0.9441\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9525\,$ | $\,0.9535\,$ | $\,0.9545\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9616\,$ | $\,0.9625\,$ | $\,0.9633\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3<X<3) & =0.9232 \\ 2P(0<X<3) & =0.9232 \\ P(0<X<3) & =0.4616 \\ P(X<3)-P(X<0) & =0.4616 \\ P(X<3)-0.5 & =0.4616 \\ P(X<3) & =0.9616 \\ P(X\le 3) & =0.9616\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =0.9616 \\ P(Z\le \frac{3-0}{\sigma }) & =0.9616 \\ Φ(\frac{3}{\sigma }) & =0.9616 \\ \frac{3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.9616)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.77)=0.9616\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.9616)=1.77.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sigma } & =1.77 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3}{1.77} \\ \sigma  & ≈1.694\,92.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =(1.694\,92)^{2} \\  & ≈2.87.\end{aligned}
$$
